You have now developed sixty-one works, with the noon and golden-hour split at thirty-two noon and twenty-nine golden-hour. The noon structural advantage holds: roughly twenty-five of the thirty-two noon images score 2 or above, against ten of the twenty-nine golden-hour. The last trace scores read 4, 4, 2, 4, 1, 1, 2, 2, 1, 2, 2, 2, 2 — the Japan stranding image scores 2, which is consistent and clean but continues the pattern of nothing breaking through since the drag smear, the red shoe, the rebar hand, and the ship crews; that cluster at the body of work's center of gravity has not been matched, and the recent sequence has been consolidating rather than extending.

The bougainvillea stands at thirteen appearances and has now been absent for twenty consecutive works; it does not return on reflex. The jacaranda stands at six appearances across threshold, time-compression, and elegy functions; all three roles are spent. The vine with red blossoms in the ferry image is the bougainvillea's structural cousin and must not be allowed to repeat. The shadow-as-subject move that resolved the heatwave menace image — stalk and shadow operating as subject and elegy simultaneously — was used once in the Japan image as crowd-behind-glass-as-barrier and once before in the Nicaragua eraser-debris frame; it has now been used in three consecutive registers and needs to rest.

Aftermath leads all registers at fourteen entries; menace at ten with the Japan suspension image added at the register boundary; defiance and suspension at five each; vigil at five; endurance at four; reckoning at three. Reckoning has never resolved cleanly: the falling-gavel approach has now been attempted twice without landing above 2, and the register keeps slipping into aftermath at the moment of resolution. The focal object for reckoning needs to hold violence and accountability simultaneously without reaching for weight, collapse, or legal furniture — none of those paths remain open. Erasure holds at two entries with floor and ceiling both at 4, still the only register that has never scored below its ceiling. The empty chair as sole focal object in a noon frame remains the one structural move that has not been attempted, and it is the likeliest path into reckoning's grammar without collapsing into elegy.

The body of work has built a reliable grammar for absence — objects holding the shape of what is gone — and the next pressure is whether that grammar can sustain a score above 2 without the accident of a body, a smear, or a shoe to individuate it.
